fields.subnational_unit: national (Nigeria), with rural and conflict-affected regions discussed
fields.population: Nigeria's national water and sanitation sector 2016-2024, compared with Ghana, Kenya, Ethiopia and South Africa
fields.sample_size: not reported (number of documents reviewed is not stated); secondary sources: Federal Ministry of Water Resources, National Bureau of Statistics, UN, WHO, UNICEF, World Bank reports and peer-reviewed articles, inclusion criteria: official or credible SDG 6 sources, last five years, Nigerian context
fields.effect_measure: qualitative content analysis of secondary documents (SRQR-reporting claimed) with a comparative assessment against four African countries
fields.effect_estimate: Nigeria's SDG 6 progress is uneven; rural and conflict-affected regions lag because of inadequate infrastructure investment, weak funding and governance inefficiency. Recommendations: enforce the National Water Resources Bill, independent monitoring bodies, performance-linked disbursement, public reporting, a fixed budget share for water, PPPs, decentralised solar systems for rural areas, adoption of practices from Ghana and South Africa. No effect estimates, no document count, no coding procedure detail.
fields.study_design: narrative qualitative review of secondary documents (not a systematic synthesis: no document count, no appraisal of sources)
fields.section: Full text (Discover Sustainability 6:1466, open access): Abstract; Method 3.1-3.4; SDG 6 targets 4; progress and governance sections; Conclusion and recommendation

evidence_level: Narrative documentary review: a qualitative review of secondary documents on Nigeria's SDG 6 progress 2016-2024 with comparison to four African countries, read in full text 2026-10-04. Governance weakness, funding gaps and weak enforcement are the stated barriers. No document count or source appraisal, no effect estimates; not an empirical test of a legal rule.
